correctness.rationale: Proposition 9 of Cai--Kiah--Nguyen--Yaakobi (arXiv:2001.01376v2) equates binary two-deletion-descendant intersections with a uniquely delimited opposite-phase alternating interval; its proof and boundary cases were read. For each fixed center the neighbor intervals correspond bijectively to nonempty subintervals of one-runs in its binary difference word. Unique run decomposition gives F=(1+R)/(1-z-zR), where R=sum_{h>=1}z^h u^{h(h+1)/2}; differentiating F at u=1 yields exact coefficients and variance. Exact direct graph comparison over all binary lengths 1..9 covers 174251 unordered center pairs; independent coefficient recurrence and rational first/second moment checks agree through length 14. Verification does not replace the general proof.

originality.rationale: The close public exact edge-enumeration result determines binary total edges \(1+(n-2)2^{n-1}\), hence only mean \(n-2+2^{1-n}\), and explicitly lists degree distribution as undetermined. The 2020 Type-A theorem and 2022 two-read graph paper provide structural adjacency and clique-cover applications, not a full degree spectrum. The new result yields the complete all-n bivariate enumerator, exact word-by-word degree, exact degree variance, and concentration; none follows from the published total-edge count alone. value.rationale: A complete graph degree spectrum is a natural and motivated exact invariant of two-read deletion reconstruction. Unlike a global edge count, it measures the distribution of each center's confusable alternatives; the all-length bivariate generating function determines all degree classes, the run formula provides per-center local ambiguity, and the exact variance \(6n+O(1)\) gives a sharp fluctuation scale. This is a complete infinite-family classification for a published coding graph, not an arbitrary sample length or a restatement of the mean degree.
